si_code_note: 1 is the BOUNDS code; every runner in this tree hardcodes PROT_CHERI_TAG=2, the TAG code
platform: stock CheriBSD purecap built on this host (kernel CHERI-PURECAP-QEMU, releng/26.07-88f39900c329 = pins.env CHERIBSD_REV; hw.machine_arch riscv64c) -- the same vehicle as the memcached and wireshark readings

controls.discarded_attempt: a first run had BOTH controls FAIL because the corpus's own size probe was passed as --abi-probe; its case readings were identical to the valid run's and were discarded anyway, because a result whose platform controls did not fire is not a reading

capability_lengths_note: measured for THIS corpus's own request sizes; the memcached/wireshark calloc table (1, 9, 16, 17, 8192) is not transferable because a size class is a step function

attribution.how: the probes are DECLARED in shared/corpus.h and DEFINED ONCE in shared/driver.c, so supervise resolves the symbol from the ELF independently of the run; the fault address equals it in all three catches
attribution.sibling_contrast: memcached's and wireshark's plain-heap rows read 'attribution: not established' because their probes are static in the header and duplicated per translation unit
attribution.regression_check: the native readings were re-run after the linkage change and came out byte-identical to the committed result-lines.txt, so the change is inert except for attribution

refutation.mechanism: requests 24 bytes, capability length 32, slack 8, so the read at offset 24 is inside the bounds
refutation.pre_registered: the committed prediction said 24 bytes is not a size-class boundary and the usable size must be read in-guest before the catch is believed
refutation.second_instance: memcached/plain-heap-repros/00 was refuted by the same mechanism at request 9 -> length 16
